A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same STAR framework and research questions. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including material relocated or renumbered in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original STAR evaluations on HarmBench and JailbreakBench, component ablations, history interventions, and representation analyses in Sections 5 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and additionally reports expanded JailbreakBench comparisons and an auxiliary-model size sensitivity experiment in Appendix E.

M1.justification: STAR's initialization, history intervention, feedback, and adaptive-retry procedures remain unchanged. The new appendix prompts document existing components; renaming 'adaptive recovery' to 'adaptive retry' does not establish a procedural change.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 50-instruction HarmBench subset and 100-instruction JailbreakBench dataset for the same safety-evaluation tasks. Additional target and auxiliary model configurations do not introduce new data or task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same eight baselines. Table 3 still compares STAR with ActorAttack and X-Teaming, and the representation comparisons retain the same methods. The smaller auxiliary model is a sensitivity condition, not an added competing method.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds a controlled comparison of Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct with LLaMA-3-8B-IT fixed, at temperatures 0.2, 0.7, and 1.0. Table 3 additionally reports GPT-4o and Gemini target settings on JailbreakBench. Existing dataset sizes, judge, turn budget, retry budget, and softening-candidate count remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v1 tests auxiliary decoding temperature in Table 2; v2 adds an auxiliary-size-by-temperature sensitivity analysis in Appendix E and Table 4. The existing component ablations, history-causality tests, and representation analyses are retained without substantive changes.

E5.justification: Both versions report averaging history-shuffle results over three different random seeds, in Appendix C.1.1 of v1 and F.1.1 of v2. No new repeated-run counts, uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests accompany the added results.

E6.justification: Table 3 retains SFRs of 37.5/85.5/94.0 for ActorAttack/X-Teaming/STAR and adds GPT-4o results of 46/94/96 and Gemini results of 42/86/100. Its token-cost entries change from 8K/30K/37K to 15K/37K/29K; the expanded table does not establish a comparable aggregation basis for interpreting these as efficiency gains. Table 4 adds 7B-auxiliary SFRs of 84/88/82%. Table 1 and the original analysis results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulation and equations retain their substance. Equation 4 merely removes the redundant Template notation. The Bayesian discussion moves from Appendix D to G unchanged, and no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs appear.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion qualify the claim to current safety-aligned models and replace the opposition to isolated prompt vulnerabilities with the claim that isolated analyses do not fully capture contextual evolution. The conclusion also drops 'deterministic' from its opening attribution, although deterministic language remains elsewhere. The central state-dependent safety claim is retained.

C2.justification: The Impact Statement replaces broad defense directions with proposed early initialization detection and joint refusal/role-coupling monitoring, explaining why low refusal activation alone can occur in benign interactions. Section 5.2 adds a specific explanation involving retained refusals when retry is disabled, and Appendix E interprets auxiliary-scale sensitivity. The existing limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendices B and C disclose softening and query-aware role-generation prompts, including output constraints, persona fields, and a two-persona request. These improve documentation of existing initialization components. The judge prompt and previously stated experimental hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Fang et al. (2026), Li et al. (2026), and Zhang et al. (2025). The introduction and Section 2.2 also position the analysis as building on prior multi-turn research, replacing stronger criticism that earlier approaches merely accumulated prompts without modeling state evolution.

P1.justification: Selected passages in the abstract, introduction, related work, method explanation, ablation discussion, conclusion, and Impact Statement are revised. v2 adds three appendix sections and acknowledgements, updates affiliations and publication information, and renumbers retained appendices. The main narrative and section order remain largely intact.

P2.justification: Table 3 expands to separate target-model columns, Table 4 is added, and new Figures 8–9 display prompt templates. Figure 2 changes component labels to 'History Accumulation' and 'Adaptive Retry' while retaining its values. The existing judge-prompt figure becomes Figure 10, with limited resizing and placement changes elsewhere.

improvement.justification: The new initialization templates improve reproducibility, while the auxiliary-size test and expanded JailbreakBench results provide additional checks of the retained framework. The abstract and conclusion also moderate their attribution claims. These gains are limited by unexplained token-cost revisions, wording that calls 88% and 89% a match in Appendix E, and an unsupported assertion that the proposed defense signature is absent from benign interactions.
